Named honestly: the EDGE is more concentrated (Gini 0.318) than the raw return, and one calendar month supplies 8.5% of it.

findings.claim: The oracle captures LESS in down months, not more - the apparent down-month advantage is entirely an artefact of buy&hold being negative there.
findings.stat: n=88 (58 up, 30 down by month-cell buy&hold sign). Raw oracle total: UP mean 10.33% (median 9.64%), DOWN mean 8.25% (median 7.63%). Edge over buy&hold: UP +5.96pp, DOWN +10.95pp - the ONLY measure on which down months win. Month range near-identical (UP 7.43%, DOWN 7.56%), so this is not a volatility difference. Capture (oracle/range): UP 1.425 vs DOWN 1.139. Path-capture (oracle / sum |daily ret|): UP 0.709 vs DOWN 0.440. Range-quartile-controlled, down months are lower in ALL FOUR quartiles (6.03 vs 6.66; 7.11 vs 8.63; 8.52 vs 10.87; 10.63 vs 15.92). Range-matched pairing (+/-1pp): 29 matched down cells, mean -2.23pp, median -2.19pp, 90% below their up-month comparators.
findings.base_rate: daily_panel: 30/88 month-cells have negative close-to-close buy&hold, mean -2.70%; the 58 positive cells mean +4.37%; overall +1.96%. Mean month path (sum |daily ret|) 15.9%.
findings.lift: Down-month EDGE is 1.84x up-month edge (10.95 vs 5.96pp) but down-month RETURN is 0.80x (8.25 vs 10.33%) and down-month path-capture is 0.62x (0.440 vs 0.709). The two lifts point opposite ways; the return-based one is the real measurement.
findings.why_not_tautology: This compares two subsets of ALREADY-selected trades against panel denominators matched on the mechanism (range, path), so selection-on-outcome applies equally to both arms and cancels. Direction survives four independent controls: raw mean, capture-on-range, capture-on-path, explicit range-matched pairing. Mechanism: a down month spends its movement on one sustained decline, which even perfect foresight cannot monetise long-only - the path is just as long but the up-legs inside it are short.

findings.claim: NDX's 38% larger oracle return than SPX is 100% explained by NDX's larger monthly range - the oracle extracts the same fraction of each index's movement.
findings.stat: n=44 months (both indices present in all). NDX oracle sum 491.6% (11.17%/mo) vs SPX 355.1% (8.07%/mo). NDX beats SPX in 44/44 months: ratio mean 1.402, median 1.395, min 1.146, max 1.823. NDX/SPX month-RANGE ratio mean 1.451, median 1.430. Ratio-of-ratios (oracle ratio / range ratio) median 0.985. corr(oracle ratio, range ratio) r = +0.752. Capture ratios near-identical: spx 1.342, ndx 1.313.
findings.base_rate: daily_panel month ranges: spx mean 6.19%, ndx mean 8.76% (ratio 1.415). Buy&hold sums: spx 73.5%, ndx 99.3% (ratio 1.35).
findings.lift: Oracle NDX/SPX = 1.40 against a range-implied 1.45; excess = -1.5% (median ratio-of-ratios 0.985). There is NO index-specific edge.
findings.why_not_tautology: Two indices, identical algorithm, each denominated by its OWN realised range from daily_panel; selection bias enters both arms identically and cancels in the ratio. A real alternative existed - NDX's higher-beta, more mean-reverting character could have made it more tractable per unit of range - and the data rejects it (0.985, indistinguishable from 1). Read: picking the higher-range instrument buys exactly its range and nothing more.

findings.claim: Every one of the 88 leg1->leg2 handoffs buys back BELOW where leg1 sold, and the dip is 2.3x-29x deeper than the same handoff at the same time gap would be at random - the second leg is a genuine re-entry on weakness. But its TIMING is indistinguishable from random.
findings.stat: n=88 leg pairs. buy2_px vs sell1_px: 88/88 negative, mean -3.88%, median -3.21%, 83% deeper than -2%. By trading-day gap: gap=0 (n=24) median -2.43%; gap=1-2 (n=18) -2.90%; gap=3-5 (n=29) -3.37%; gap>=6 (n=17) -6.06%. Time gap distribution: median 3 trading days, mean 3.25, 27.3% same-day, 38.6% within 1 day.
findings.base_rate: daily_panel low(t+g)/high(t)-1 over all same-month day pairs: g=0 n=1817, 100% negative, median -1.04%; g=1 n=1729, 92%, -0.84%; g=2 n=1641, 76%, -0.75%; g=3 n=1553, 70%, -0.66%; g=5 n=1377, 59%, -0.46%; g=8 n=1113, 53%, -0.21%. Time-gap null (Monte Carlo, 2,000 random valid placements per month with the ACTUAL hold lengths held fixed): P(gap=0)=27.2%, P(gap<=1)=46.8%, median gap 2.
findings.lift: Price: gap=0 -2.43% vs base -1.04% (2.3x deeper); gap=3-5 -3.37% vs ~-0.55% (6x); gap>=6 -6.06% vs -0.21% (29x), the multiple growing with the gap. Timing: observed P(gap=0)=27.3% vs null 27.2% = ZERO lift; P(gap<=1)=38.6% vs null 46.8% - the oracle in fact waits LONGER than random.
findings.why_not_tautology: '100% negative' is largely mechanical - buying an intraday low after selling an intraday high is negative with zero drift, and the g=0 base rate is also 100%. Naming that is the point. The finding survives because the base rate is computed at the SAME time gap from the same panel and the oracle's dip is 2.3x-29x deeper than that mechanical floor. The complementary null result is what makes it interpretable: the second entry's CALENDAR position is exactly random once hold lengths are fixed, so the handoff is defined by price level, not by timing.

findings.claim: The 23 same-day round trips sit at the 97th percentile of intraday range - and are the oracle's cheapest return (13% of legs, 8.2% of total). Across all hold lengths the oracle beats a random same-length window by a flat ~2.8x, not a rising multiple.
findings.stat: n=23 same-day legs (13.1% of 176); their returns ARE that day's intraday range: mean 3.02%, median 2.88%, min 1.33%, max 5.12%. Percentile against all 1,817 panel days: median 97.2, mean 93.7, min 68.7; 74% above the 90th percentile. They supply 69.4 of 846.7pp = 8.2%. Split spx 14 / ndx 9. Hold-bucket returns: h=0 mean 3.02% (n=23), h=1-3 4.31% (n=39), h=4-7 4.09% (n=60), h=8-14 6.37% (n=45), h=15+ 8.59% (n=9); 8-14 day holds are 26% of legs but 33.8% of return. Median hold 5.0, mean 5.97, max 21.
findings.base_rate: daily_panel intraday range across all 1,817 days: mean 1.22%, median 1.05%, p90 2.02%, max 12.66%. Same-month low->high windows of length h: h=1 mean 1.30% (n=1729), h=2 1.40% (n=1641), h=3 1.51% (n=1553), h=5 1.73% (n=1377), h=7 1.92% (n=1201), h=10 2.20% (n=937), h=14 2.70% (n=587).
findings.lift: Same-day legs: 2.5x the mean daily range and above the all-day 90th percentile. By hold length the oracle's mean is 2.2x-3.7x the same-length base rate (h=0 2.5x, h=1 3.3x, h=2 3.7x, h=3 2.4x, h=5 2.2x, h=7 2.3x, h=10 2.6x, h=14 3.4x) - roughly FLAT at ~2.8x, i.e. scale-invariant in holding time.
findings.why_not_tautology: Directly tautological: a same-day oracle leg IS 'the widest-range day available', so a high range percentile is definitional. It is reported to price that tautology - those days, drawn from the top 3% of the range distribution, still return LESS (3.02%) than every longer hold bucket. Separating a real effect would require showing those days are identifiable ex ante (high VIX, gap open, opex); NOT tested, and the data has NO event calendar (no FOMC/CPI/NFP dates), so the obvious explanation cannot be checked here. The flat ~2.8x multiple across hold lengths is the less tautological half: the oracle's advantage over a random same-length window does not grow with time held.

findings.claim: The oracle converts a stable ~62% of each month's total absolute price movement into return, but path is a WORSE predictor than range - meaning it is not harvesting chop.
findings.stat: n=88 cells. oracle_total / month path (sum |daily ret_1d_pct|): mean 0.617, median 0.614, sd 0.176 (CV 29%), min 0.322, max 1.140. Correlation with path r=+0.775 vs r=+0.879 for range. Path-efficiency is the measure on which up and down months separate most sharply (0.709 vs 0.440).
findings.base_rate: daily_panel month path mean 15.9% per month-cell; month range mean 7.47%; buy&hold mean 1.96% - a typical month travels ~8x its net move and ~2.1x its range.
findings.lift: Oracle banks 0.617 of path vs buy&hold's 1.96/15.9 = 0.123 - a 5.0x lift in path conversion. Ceiling reference: 1.0 would require catching every daily swing, impossible with two legs.
findings.why_not_tautology: Selection drives this hard - the oracle picks the two highest-signed-content segments, so a high path-share is near-definitional. Reported because the COMPARISON is informative: path predicts oracle return worse than range does (r 0.775 vs 0.879), so a month of many small oscillations yields the oracle less than one clean round trip of the same total path. Separating this from pure selection would mean testing whether path-efficiency is predictable from the PRIOR month's path; not run.

dead_ends: LEG1 DOES NOT PREFER THE START OF THE MONTH. 62% of leg-1 buys land in the first 3 trading days - striking against the daily_panel base rate of 10% of all days - but a Monte Carlo null that places both legs randomly while holding the ACTUAL hold lengths fixed gives 61%. Lift +1pp on n=88. The clustering is entirely a packing constraint (two non-overlapping ~5-day legs in a ~21-day month), not a calendar effect.

MONTH-END SELLING IS ALMOST ALL MECHANICAL. 74% of leg-2 sells land in the last 3 trading days vs 61% under the same random-placement null (n=88). +13pp is real but small, was tested alongside the month-start hypothesis, and offers no separation from the same packing constraint.

TRADING DAYS IN MONTH DOES NOT MATTER. corr(oracle month total, tdays in month) r = +0.158 (n=88). A 23-day month gives the oracle essentially nothing over a 19-day one - opportunity is set by range, not by how many bars exist.

DAY-OF-WEEK IS NOISE. Buy-date weekday counts over 176 legs: Mon 41, Tue 25, Wed 38, Thu 37, Fri 35, against daily_panel bases of Mon 342 / Tue 377 / Wed 373 / Thu 362 / Fri 363 of 1,817 (expected ~33-37 each). Monday +8, Tuesday -12 on n=176 across 5 simultaneously-tested categories. Nothing survives.

VIX ADDS NOTHING OVER REALISED RANGE. Mean monthly VIX correlates with oracle month total at Pearson +0.566 but Spearman only +0.260 (n=88) - the linear fit is carried almost entirely by April 2025. Realised range (+0.879) and realised vol (+0.835) dominate. This is precisely why the range finding cannot be converted into a forward-looking rule without an out-of-sample test.

THE TWO LEGS OF A MONTH ARE NOT LINKED. corr(leg1 return, leg2 return) within the same month-cell r = +0.220 (n=88); leg2 exceeds leg1 in 53% of months; identical median holds (5.0 days each). There is no 'first leg sets up the second' structure - they are near-independent draws on the same month's volatility.

Base rate 167/1817 = 9.19% — correct. RSI<30: n=84 (4.62% of days), 25 buys, precision 29.76%, recall 25/167 = 14.97%, lift 3.24x — every figure matches to the decimal. MULTIPLE COMPARISONS: survives. Under independence, expected hits = 84 x 0.0919 = 7.72, sd 2.65, observed 25, z = 6.5 — that clears 70-fold Bonferroni by a wide margin. WHY IT STILL DIES — RULE 3, and harder than the agent admits: RSI<30 is entirely subsumed by the raw price-lowness flag is_20d_low, which is a mechanical restatement of "the oracle buys at a local price low," true by construction of the oracle. Head-to-head, is_20d_low strictly dominates RSI<30 on every axis: n=139, precision 35.97%, recall 29.9%, lift 3.91x — better precision, double the recall, higher lift, with zero indicator machinery. So the claim's own self-assessment ("largely tautological") understates it. It is not largely tautological, it is wholly tautological: RSI14 is a monotone function of recent price, the oracle selects local price minima by construction, and the 3.24x lift is a re-description of that construction with no residual information. Per Rule 3 this is exactly the named failure mode — "buys happen at low RSI" here means only "rallies start from lows." Note also Rule 4: nothing here is a strategy, and no out-of-sample test (forward returns from RSI<30 entries on held-out data) has been run. Scripts under /home/user/INMA-/research-vault/backtest/scratch/verify_rsi.py, verify2.py, verify3.py, verify4.py. Nothing dropped, full Jan-2023 to Aug-2026 window, both indices.

CLUSTERING/POWER: the agent's own caveat is real but I tested it and it does not kill the result. WHAT I DID BREAK (framing, not the statistic): (1) Horizon fragility — at 21d the ordering inverts. Base rate 167/1817 = 9.19% (176 trades but only 167 unique (sym,buy_date) pairs; 9 buy dates carry two legs — the panel-binary construction handles this correctly, and their 9.19% shows they did it right, not 176/1817). is_20d_low: 139/1817 = 7.65% of days, P(buy)=50/139=35.97%, lift 3.91x. Inside that stratum: rsi<30 24/59=40.68%, rsi>=30 26/80=32.50%, diff +8.18pp, ratio 1.252x. Standalone rsi<30 25/84=29.76%, lift 3.24x. dd<-5% stratum: 27/119=0.227 vs 9/69=0.130, ratio 1.74x (they said 1.75x — rounding). Nothing is wrong.

THE CORE CLAIM IS UNDERSTATED, NOT OVERSTATED. Outside the local-low stratum RSI<30 is 1/25 = 4.0% vs rsi>=30 116/1653 = 7.0% — ratio 0.57x, i.e. mildly ANTI-predictive. RSI's entire standalone 3.24x lift is carried by the 59 of 84 RSI<30 days (70%) that are also 20-day lows. Reverse the conditioning and the asymmetry is stark: within rsi<30, is_20d_low gives 24/59=40.7% vs 1/25=4.0%, a 10.2x marginal. is_20d_low absorbs RSI; RSI does not absorb is_20d_low. That is the claim, sharper.

THE +8.2pp IS NOISE. Naive SE of the difference = 0.083, z = 0.99, 95% CI on the difference [-8.0pp, +24.4pp], on the ratio roughly [0.75x, 1.75x] — straddles 1.0. It also fails to replicate across indices: SPX 10/31=0.323 vs 18/40=0.450 (0.72x, wrong sign), NDX 14/28=0.500 vs 8/40=0.200 (2.50x). The whole +8.2pp is one index. A threshold sweep inside the stratum (<25/<30/<35/<40/<45 → 1.39x/1.25x/0.97x/1.09x/0.77x) oscillates around 1 with no monotone structure, and shows 30 was not cherry-picked to flatter RSI (<25 would have looked better).

MULTIPLE COMPARISONS DO NOT APPLY IN THE THREATENING DIRECTION. This is a deflationary finding — it says an apparently-strong variable collapses under conditioning. Testing 70 hypotheses inflates false POSITIVES; it makes an agent more likely to report the raw 3.24x standalone RSI lift, not less. This claim is the correction to that artifact, not an instance of it, so it is not exposed to the usual MC discount.

SELECTION-ON-OUTCOME. Yes, entirely — and naming it IS the finding, per Rule 3. The self-assessment of "high" is the correct call, not a dodge. The residual caveat that stands: 139 days is only ~49 distinct episodes (gap<=3d merge; 24 episodes in the rsi<30 arm, 46 in the rsi>=30 arm), and SPX/NDX are near-duplicate series, so effective n is well below 139.
